summary: Roland Grubb Kent was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Swarthmore, Berlin, Munich, Athens, and Pennsylvania (Ph.D. 1903), he taught comparative philology at Pennsylvania (1902–1947) and founded the Linguistic Society of America.

Roland Harweg was a linguist who studied under Alfred Schmitt and Peter Hartmann. He held academic posts at the University of Münster (circa 1962–1969) and the Ruhr University Bochum (circa 1969–1999).
Roland Knyvet Wilson was an Indologist who completed his B.A. at the University of Cambridge around 1859–1863. He later served as Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge from 1884 to 1893.
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Marburg, attested in 2002.

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate at Salzburg and habilitated at Heidelberg. He held posts at the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient, Humboldt University, and Heidelberg, before becoming a professor and director at the University of Munich.

Rolf Alfred Stein worked in Tibetology and sinology, studying under scholars including Pelliot, Maspero, and Granet in Paris. He held major posts at the EFEO, INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Hiersche worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Jena and under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle. He held posts at Humboldt University, the Free University of Berlin, Lille, and the University of Giessen (1970–1989).

Rolf Scheuermann works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, he held positions at Vienna, Leipzig, Heidelberg, the University of Munich, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.

Romain Rolland worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Paris, he held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, EPHE, and the University of Paris.

Roman Ghirshman was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and the Louvre, he directed the Louvre (1931–1972) and held posts with DAFA, IFAO, and Aix-Marseille University.

Roman Jakobson was a linguist who studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński at Moscow University and later at the German University of Prague. He held major academic posts at Masaryk University, Harvard University, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who completed her doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She taught at Kurukshetra University and the University of Delhi before serving as Professor of Ancient Indian History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991).
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. He served as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland, attested in 1998, and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (circa 1989–1997) and San Francisco State University (circa 1997).

Ronald Egan is a sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held academic positions at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara (circa 1993–2012), and Stanford University.

Ronald Eric Emmerick specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Sydney, Cambridge (under H. W. Bailey), and Oxford, later teaching at SOAS and serving as professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).
Ronald Herman Poelmeijer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam. He served as Lecturer of Tibetan at Leiden University from circa 1987 to 1993.
Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who served at the University of Chicago, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.
